name: Alchemist
summary: A Universal World Class any character may take regardless of their class. It levels through the bench — dissolving, reacting and sealing — unlocking the laboratory's verbs and higher tiers of material, from brimstone and saltpetre to dragon bile and philosophic mercury.
_namespace_note: This is the alchemist WORLD CLASS (rules.worldclass.get / rules.alchemist), not the PF1e Alchemist character class in content/classes/ (rules.classes.get). They share a name and nothing else: a Rogue is an Alchemist here the way a Fighter is an Herbalist — by doing the work. The two namespaces never meet in code.
_thresholds_note: The Herbalist's curve, unchanged, because the two tracks pay mastery the same way (rules/worldclass.py MP_AWARDS is shared) and a chain here is worth what a chain there is worth. The dip at level 4 is the Herbalist's deliberate dip; see herbalist.json for the measured pacing that produced it — do not 'fix' it in one file and not the other.
_deeds_note: The same trap the Herbalist's deed walked into is avoided the same way: the deed is the MATERIAL, not the method. If the deed required catalyze — a Level 5 method — the gate could never open. Any successful craft at legendary tier is the great work, however it was reached, and catalyze is the mastery that follows it.

legendary-work.note: Any successful craft at legendary tier, however it was reached.

levels.note: Roadside work: burning to ash, dissolving in a jar, corking the result.
Real glassware: separating a mixture into what it was hiding.
The dangerous heart of the craft: making substances fight, and living through it.
The slow furnace: vapour to crystal, matter refined past what a flame can do.
The great work: catalysts that transform without being consumed.

method_descriptions.calcine: Roasts a material in the crucible until only its essential salt remains. Strips water and rot; the ash keeps indefinitely.
method_descriptions.dissolve: Takes a material up into a solvent so it can be worked as a liquid. Most chains start here — the bench works solutions, not lumps.
method_descriptions.seal: Closes the work into its vessel: flask, bladder or clay pot. The finishing method — nothing follows a seal, and an unsealed preparation is bench-work, not an item you can carry and throw.
method_descriptions.filter: Passes a solution through frame and paper, holding back what does not belong. Removes impurities, penalties and secondary toxicities while keeping the beneficial traits.
method_descriptions.precipitate: Drives a dissolved substance back out of its solvent as a concentrated solid. The reverse of dissolve, and the way a solution becomes a powder worth keeping.
method_descriptions.react: Sets two prepared substances against each other and keeps what the violence produces. The heart of the craft: +25% to the primary effect, and every classic of the trade — fire that clings, acid that eats, smoke that blinds — is a reaction. A reaction needs a solvent as its medium.
method_descriptions.stabilize: Buffers a reaction so it spends itself in the product instead of in your face. Required before two volatile materials may share a vessel, and the only answer to a material that attacks its own flask.
method_descriptions.sublime: Vaporises a substance in the athanor and recovers it as crystal, leaving everything gross behind. +25% to the primary effect; the exotic tiers are worked almost entirely as sublimates.
method_descriptions.catalyze: Uses legendary material to drive a transformation it does not take part in. Permanent works, philosophic salts, and preparations at 150% of base strength.

_portable_note: The laboratory and athanor are furniture. Whether a chain can be attempted is therefore partly a question about where the character is standing, which is scene state rather than sheet state — the same split herbalist.json declares for its still and workbench.
